description: Looking for enthusiastic teammates who are excited to explore ideas, work together and create something meaningful! If you're interested in space, technology, storytelling or creative problem-solving, let's team up! All skill levels are welcome. Let's learn, collaborate and make this challenge exciting together! 🚀
summary:
We built Still Listening-for our project Aakaasham, an interactive scrollytelling story with a companion slide deck. You play a radio signal leaving Earth and meet the hardware NASA left behind: Apollo landers, moon buggies and laser mirrors on the Moon, then Viking, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity on Mars. At a fork, you choose between answering Opportunity in its 2018 dust storm and following Pioneer 10 into deep space. Each path ends in an epilogue on other machines that went quiet, including InSight, Kepler, NEAR Shoemaker and Dawn. The page uses animated line art, parallax and a color palette that shifts with each chapter.

It turns dry mission facts into a personal journey, so people learn through exploration and choice instead of a list. It reframes “dead” spacecraft as lasting legacies that still shape science. This matters because it makes space history emotional, accessible and memorable for general audiences. It is also designed to be inclusive, with readable type, reduced-motion support and mobile layouts.
It answers Abandoned but Not Forgotten by treating NASA’s discarded equipment as characters, not junk. Mirrors still work, rovers outlived their 90-day missions, and a helicopter built for five flights flew 72. Each silent machine taught engineers how to build the next one, so what was left behind is remembered.
details:
Still Listening is an interactive scrollytelling website about NASA hardware left on the Moon and Mars. The reader is a radio signal leaving Earth, and scrolling moves them through five chapters: the Moon (Apollo landers, moon buggies, laser mirrors, Surveyor 3), Mars (Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Ingenuity), a choice at a fork, then an epilogue. At the fork the reader picks between answering Opportunity in its 2018 dust storm and following Pioneer 10 into deep space. Each path ends with other machines that went quiet: InSight, Kepler, NEAR Shoemaker and Dawn. A companion 7-slide deck summarizes the story.

Benefits and intended impact
It turns dry mission facts into a personal journey, so people learn through exploration and choice. It reframes “abandoned” spacecraft as lasting legacies that still shape science, and it makes space history emotional, accessible and memorable, especially for young space fans.

Tools and technology
HTML, CSS and JavaScript; GSAP with ScrollTrigger for scroll animation; HTML Canvas for the particle background; hand-drawn inline SVG illustrations; Google Fonts (Fraunces and Atkinson Hyperlegible); GitHub and GitHub Pages for hosting. No special hardware was needed. Mission facts come from NASA’s Space Science Data Coordinated Archive and science.nasa.gov. Add any other tools your team used.

Creativity
The reader is the radio signal, so the story is told from a new point of view. The branching choice means no two journeys are identical. Line-art illustrations draw themselves as you scroll, and the color palette and background motion change with each chapter.

Factors we considered
Accuracy of mission facts, accessibility (readable fonts, reduced-motion support, high contrast), mobile-friendly layouts, no installs or logins, and a clear, age-friendly tone.
